subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Cosmic Web
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Cosmic Web.

hook.text: Galaxies aren't scattered randomly. They form filaments, walls, and clusters—a vast web stretching across the cosmos.

buildup.text: Dark matter acts as scaffolding. Galaxies formed along dense filaments, leaving enormous voids between them.

discovery.text: Computer simulations match the observed web perfectly. The pattern was set by quantum wobbles in the infant universe.

twist.text: The largest voids are hundreds of millions of light-years across—nearly empty of galaxies. Cosmic deserts.

climax.text: Mapping the cosmic web reveals the universe's largest structures and confirms how gravity shapes everything.

punchline.text: Galaxies on threads. Voids between them. The universe has architecture.

quiz.question: What role does dark matter play in the cosmic web?
options: It acts as invisible scaffolding along which galaxies formed
It fills the voids between galaxy filaments
It repels galaxies to create the web pattern

details.summary: The cosmic web is the universe's largest-scale structure — a network of galaxy-filled filaments, dense nodes where filaments intersect, and vast empty voids between them.
details.whyItMatters: The cosmic web reveals the universe's underlying skeleton. Its structure matches predictions of how dark matter and gravity shaped the distribution of all matter, confirming our understanding of cosmic evolution from the Big Bang to today.
takeaways: Galaxies cluster along filaments forming a cosmic web structure
Nodes where filaments meet contain massive galaxy clusters
The pattern grew from tiny Big Bang density fluctuations

faq.question: How big are cosmic voids?
faq.answer: Typical voids span 30-300 million light-years across and are mostly empty of galaxies. The Boötes void is one of the largest known, spanning 330 million light-years. Voids aren't completely empty — they contain sparse galaxies — but they're dramatically underdense compared to filaments.

faq.question: Can we see the cosmic web directly?
faq.answer: Mapping galaxy positions reveals the web's filamentary structure. More directly, astronomers have imaged filaments through their faint emission of Lyman-alpha radiation (hydrogen glow) and through absorption of light from background quasars.
